title: Great Barrier Reef Legislation Amendment Bill 2014
short_title: Great Barrier Reef Legislation Amendment Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would restrict port development affecting the Great Barrier Reef World Heritage Area and prohibit dumping dredged material within that protected area.
It would impose an approval moratorium from 13 February 2014 until a strategic assessment was completed and considered adequate by the World Heritage Committee.
The bill would commence on Royal Assent, with retrospective rules preventing permits or approvals after 31 December 2013 for the prohibited dredged material activities.
changes: New ports would be prohibited outside existing port areas and in specified protected locations.
Existing port developments would be barred where individual or cumulative impacts affected the area's world heritage values.
Developments without a net benefit for the protected area could not be approved.
Dumping dredged material would attract up to 250 penalty units, 12 months' imprisonment, or both.
Knowingly or recklessly loading dredged material for dumping in the area would also be an offence.
summary.affected: People proposing port developments, dumping dredged material or loading it for dumping in the protected area are affected.
